statement: The singular value decomposition (SVD) of an $m \times n$ complex matrix $\mathbf{M}$ is a factorization $\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{U} \mathbf{\Sigma} \mathbf{V}^*$, where $\mathbf{U}$ is an $m \times m$ unitary matrix, $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ is an $m \times n$ rectangular diagonal matrix with non-negative real singular values on the diagonal, and $\mathbf{V}$ is an $n \times n$ unitary matrix (with $\mathbf{V}^*$ denoting its conjugate transpose).

symbols.meaning: rectangular diagonal matrix containing singular values
number of non-zero eigenvalues of M^* M
diagonal positive definite matrix containing non-zero eigenvalues of M^* M

properties.property: The singular value decomposition factorizes $\mathbf{M}$ into a rotation, followed by a scaling, followed by another rotation, generalizing eigendecomposition to non-square matrices.
properties.why: Unitary matrices act as rotations/reflections and $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ scales along coordinate axes

properties.property: The right-singular vectors in $\mathbf{V}$ are eigenvectors of $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$, satisfying $\mathbf{V}^* \mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M} \mathbf{V} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{D} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.
properties.why: $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$ is Hermitian and positive semi-definite and thus unitarily diagonalizable by the spectral theorem

properties.property: The non-zero singular values of $\mathbf{M}$ are the square roots of the non-zero eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$.
properties.why: The diagonal block of non-zero singular values in $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ is $\mathbf{D}^{\frac{1}{2}}$

properties.property: The left-singular vectors corresponding to non-zero singular values satisfy $\mathbf{U}_1 = \mathbf{M} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{D}^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ and form an orthonormal set ($\mathbf{U}_1^* \mathbf{U}_1 = \mathbf{I}_1$).
Vectors $\mathbf{V}_2$ corresponding to zero eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$ lie in the null space of $\mathbf{M}$, satisfying $\mathbf{M} \mathbf{V}_2 = \mathbf{0}$.
The number of non-zero singular values $\ell$ satisfies $\ell \le \min(n, m)$.
properties.why: $\ell$ is the dimension of the positive definite diagonal block $\mathbf{D}$ of eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$

properties.property: Singular values can be variationally characterized as maxima of $\sigma(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}) = \mathbf{u}^\mathsf{T} \mathbf{M} \mathbf{v}$ over unit spheres $S^{m-1} \times S^{n-1}$, and are non-negative.
properties.why: Continuous functions attain maxima on compact sets, and flipping vector signs would make any negative value positive and strictly larger

assumptions.assumption: $\mathbf{M}$ is a finite-dimensional $m \times n$ matrix with real or complex entries.
assumptions.breaks_when: The operator is infinite-dimensional or entries are not over the real or complex field.

failure_modes.signature: Diagonal entries of $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ become zero for indices $j > \ell$, with $\ell < \min(n, m)$.
failure_modes.cause: $\mathbf{M}^* \mathbf{M}$ has non-trivial null space, producing zero eigenvalues and corresponding right singular vectors $\mathbf{V}_2$ such that $\mathbf{M} \mathbf{V}_2 = \mathbf{0}$.
